indication: Newly diagnosed stage III/IV classical Hodgkin lymphoma (CD30-positive)

drugs.special_instructions: VESICANT — intravenous bolus over 10 minutes. Maximum lifetime cumulative dose 450 mg/m² (400 mg/m² if prior mediastinal/pericardial radiotherapy). Discontinue if cardiac failure develops. Administer as part of AVD before brentuximab vedotin.

Intravenous bolus in 50ml sodium chloride 0.9% over 10 minutes. Dose rounded to nearest 1mg. No maximum dose cap in this protocol. VESICANT — NPSA/2008/RRR04 must be followed for IV vinca alkaloid administration. Administer as part of AVD before brentuximab vedotin.

VESICANT — Intravenous infusion in 500ml sodium chloride 0.9% over 60 minutes. PROTECT FROM LIGHT. May cause pain at infusion site — adjust infusion rate or volume if necessary. Administer last of AVD drugs before brentuximab vedotin.

drugs.timing: Approximately 1 hour after end of dacarbazine infusion
drugs.special_instructions: Intravenous infusion in 100ml sodium chloride 0.9% over 30 minutes. MUST be administered AFTER completion of AVD, starting approximately 1 hour after end of dacarbazine infusion. Dose capped at 120mg. Dose banded per national dose bands.

drugs.frequency: Once daily, days and duration at clinician discretion
drugs.special_instructions: G-CSF may be considered in patients at higher risk of febrile neutropenia, at the discretion of the treating clinician. Not mandated on the Echelon-1 clinical trial. Use filgrastim or lenograstim per local policy.

pre_medications.special_instructions: May be given orally if IV access not yet established.
NK1 antagonist antiemetic on days 1 and 15.
Antiemetic pre-medication: dexamethasone 8mg on days 1 and 15. May be given IV if required.

rescue_medications.special_instructions: For brentuximab vedotin infusion-related reactions. For subsequent infusions if prior reaction: premedicate with chlorphenamine 10mg IV, hydrocortisone 100mg IV and paracetamol 1000mg oral.
For brentuximab vedotin infusion-related reactions or anaphylaxis.
When required for the treatment of brentuximab vedotin infusion-related reactions. Maximum dose 4000mg/24 hours. Check if patient has already taken paracetamol before administering.
When required for the relief of brentuximab vedotin-related bronchospasm.

take_home_medicines.timing: Starting on the evening of the day of chemotherapy (day 1 and day 15)
take_home_medicines.frequency: Twice daily for 3 days starting on the evening of each treatment day
take_home_medicines.special_instructions: Take-home antiemetic: ondansetron 8mg twice daily for 3 days. First dose on the evening of each treatment day (day 1 and day 15).
Take-home NK1 antiemetic: aprepitant 80mg once daily on days 2, 3, 16 and 17 (the 2 days after each treatment day).
Take-home antiemetic: dexamethasone 4mg once daily on days 2, 3, 16 and 17 (the 2 days after each treatment day). Take with or after food.

take_home_medicines.frequency: Three times daily when required for nausea
take_home_medicines.special_instructions: Take as required for nausea after each treatment day.

take_home_medicines.frequency: Once daily on Monday, Wednesday and Friday for 28 days
take_home_medicines.special_instructions: PCP prophylaxis: co-trimoxazole 960mg once daily on Monday, Wednesday and Friday for 28 days per cycle. Continue for three months after final dose of BV-AVD.
Antiviral prophylaxis: aciclovir 400mg twice daily for 28 days per cycle. Continue for three months after final dose of BV-AVD.
Tumour lysis prophylaxis: allopurinol 300mg once daily for 7 days — cycle 1 only.

take_home_medicines.frequency: 4mg initially then 2mg after each loose stool when required for diarrhoea
take_home_medicines.special_instructions: Loperamide 4mg initially then 2mg after each loose stool when required for diarrhoea.

dose_modifications.description: Grade 2 peripheral neuropathy: reduce brentuximab vedotin to 0.9 mg/kg (maximum 90mg).
dose_modifications.action_text: Reduce brentuximab vedotin to 0.9 mg/kg max 90mg (grade 2 neuropathy)

dose_modifications.description: Grade 3 peripheral neuropathy: withhold brentuximab vedotin until ≤grade 2, then resume at 0.9 mg/kg (maximum 90mg).
dose_modifications.action_text: Withhold brentuximab vedotin until ≤grade 2, then resume at 0.9 mg/kg max 90mg

dose_modifications.description: Hepatic impairment Child-Pugh A, B or C: reduce brentuximab vedotin to 0.9 mg/kg (maximum 90mg).
dose_modifications.action_text: Reduce brentuximab vedotin to 0.9 mg/kg max 90mg (Child-Pugh A/B/C)

dose_modifications.description: Renal impairment CrCl <30 ml/min: reduce brentuximab vedotin to 0.9 mg/kg (maximum 90mg).
dose_modifications.action_text: Reduce brentuximab vedotin to 0.9 mg/kg max 90mg (CrCl <30 ml/min)

dose_modifications.description: Renal impairment CrCl 45-60 ml/min: reduce dacarbazine to 80%.
Renal impairment CrCl 30-44 ml/min: reduce dacarbazine to 75%.
Renal impairment CrCl <30 ml/min: reduce dacarbazine to 70%.
Hepatic impairment: bilirubin <30 µmol/L AND AST/ALT 2-3×ULN — reduce doxorubicin to 75%.
Hepatic impairment: bilirubin 22-50 µmol/L and/or more than 3×ULN — reduce doxorubicin to 50%
Hepatic impairment: AST/ALT more than 3×ULN (regardless of bilirubin) — reduce doxorubicin to 50%. Per PDF: bilirubin 22-50 and/or more than 3×ULN.
Hepatic impairment: bilirubin 51-86 µmol/L — reduce doxorubicin to 25%.
Hepatic impairment: bilirubin >86 µmol/L or Child-Pugh C — omit doxorubicin.
dose_modifications.action_text: Omit doxorubicin (bilirubin >86 µmol/L or Child-Pugh C)

dose_modifications.description: Hepatic impairment: bilirubin 22-51 µmol/L — reduce vinblastine to 75%.
Hepatic impairment: bilirubin >51 µmol/L — reduce vinblastine to 50%.
NCI-CTC grade 2 motor or grade 3 sensory neurotoxicity: reduce vinblastine dose to 3mg/m². For higher toxicity grades or if toxicity increases despite reduction, stop vinblastine.
dose_modifications.action_text: Reduce vinblastine to 3mg/m² (grade 2 motor or grade 3 sensory neuropathy). Stop for higher grades.

dose_modifications.description: NCI-CTC grade 3 sensory neurotoxicity: reduce vinblastine dose to 3mg/m². For higher toxicity grades or if toxicity increases despite reduction, stop vinblastine.
dose_modifications.action_text: Reduce vinblastine to 3mg/m² (grade 3 sensory neuropathy). Stop for higher grades.

dose_modifications.description: Dacarbazine is activated and metabolised in the liver and can be hepatotoxic. Consider dose reduction or omission in severe hepatic impairment.
dose_modifications.action_text: Consider dacarbazine dose reduction or omission in severe hepatic impairment

dose_modifications.description: Renal impairment CrCl <10 ml/min: consider dose reduction of doxorubicin in severe renal failure.

hematological_toxicity_rules.additional_notes: UHS B-AVD protocol: 'Deliver on time and at full dose regardless of haematological counts unless there is an overriding clinical reason not to do so.' Any dose modifications or delays must be discussed and approved by the responsible consultant. G-CSF is at clinician discretion — not mandated.

UHS B-AVD protocol: 'Deliver on time and at full dose regardless of haematological counts unless there is an overriding clinical reason not to do so.' Any dose modifications or delays must be discussed and approved by the responsible consultant.

non_hematological_toxicity_rules.action_text: Grade 2 peripheral neuropathy: reduce brentuximab vedotin to 0.9 mg/kg (max 90mg). Grade 3: withhold until ≤grade 2 then resume at 0.9 mg/kg. Grade 4: permanently discontinue.
If anaphylaxis occurs, immediately and permanently discontinue brentuximab vedotin. For grade 1-2 reactions, interrupt infusion and manage symptomatically; premedicate for subsequent infusions.
Discontinue doxorubicin if cardiac failure develops. Monitor cumulative dose — do not exceed lifetime maximum.

treatment_delay_criteria.delay_until: NOT APPLICABLE — deliver on time regardless of haematological counts unless overriding clinical reason
treatment_delay_criteria.action_if_not_recovered: UHS B-AVD protocol states to deliver on time and at full dose regardless of haematological counts unless there is an overriding clinical reason. Any dose modifications or delays must be discussed and approved by the responsible consultant.

baseline_requirements.timing: Before starting doxorubicin in patients with cardiac history, cardiac risk factors, or elderly
Before cycle 1 — CD30 positivity required for brentuximab vedotin eligibility
Before day 1 and day 15 of each cycle

pre_cycle_labs.timing: Before day 1 and day 15 of each cycle
Before every dose of brentuximab vedotin
Before cycle 1 if cardiac history or risk factors

monitoring: FBC, U&Es, and LFTs before day 1 and day 15 of each cycle
Peripheral neuropathy assessment before every dose of brentuximab vedotin
Brentuximab vedotin infusion monitoring for infusion-related reactions
Cumulative doxorubicin dose reviewed before every cycle
LVEF monitoring in patients with cardiac risk factors
Monitor for pulmonary toxicity symptoms throughout treatment
Monitor for new neurological or cognitive symptoms (PML surveillance)
G-CSF may be considered at clinician discretion in patients at higher risk of febrile neutropenia
warnings: G-CSF may be considered in patients at higher risk of febrile neutropenia at the discretion of the treating clinician. Not mandated on the Echelon-1 clinical trial. B-AVD carries a significantly higher risk of febrile neutropenia than ABVD.
Brentuximab vedotin is associated with peripheral neuropathy — assess before every cycle.
Maximum lifetime cumulative doxorubicin dose: 450 mg/m² (400 mg/m² if prior mediastinal/pericardial radiotherapy).
TA-GvHD risk: irradiated blood products required for all Hodgkin lymphoma patients.
Monitor for pulmonary toxicity (unlike ABVD, bleomycin is NOT used in this regimen).
Dacarbazine — protect from light. May cause pain at infusion site.
Brentuximab vedotin must be administered AFTER AVD completion, approximately 1 hour after dacarbazine ends.
CD30 positivity (immunohistochemistry) must be confirmed before brentuximab vedotin — not licensed for CD30-negative disease.
Risk of progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML) with brentuximab vedotin — monitor for new neurological or cognitive symptoms throughout treatment.

Stevens-Johnson syndrome (SJS) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN) have been reported with brentuximab vedotin. Monitor skin reactions closely — withhold brentuximab vedotin if serious muco-cutaneous reaction suspected until resolved, or discontinue.

required_patient_fields.platelet_count: Required for cycle safety check on day 1 and day 15

required_patient_fields.bilirubin: Required for doxorubicin and vinblastine dose modification
